title: The Red door of the barn
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：red　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 red 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the painter wrote of ① a red door of the barn in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② more red than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the red ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most red door of the barn anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1981 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too red to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the red ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a red face of the boy, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as red as the face of the boy they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was red or not, and he said so.

By 1994 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something red, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite red; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the red ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1997, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another red door of the barn in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ more red than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most red face of the boy in the whole studio, she said in 1999, was the one she could never quite name; the red ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 红色（前置定语 a red door of the barn：1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件红色的红门）
B. adj. 红色／涨红（比较级 more red than：文中两处，一处比谷仓的红门，一处比预想）
C. adj. 红色／涨红（最高级 the most red：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 红色（表语 too red to do：母亲觉得它太红色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 涨红（前置定语 a red face of the boy：叔叔把整件事称作一桩涨红的脸）
F. adj. 涨红（同级比较 as red as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩男孩涨红的脸相比）
G. adj. 涨红（后置定语 something red：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 涨红（受程度副词修饰 quite red：那位观者的评价）

items.q: a red door of the barn
the most red door of the barn anybody
a red face of the boy
The most red face of the boy in

answers.why: red 意为“红色”，1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件红色的红门”，此处作前置定语 a red door of the barn。
red 意为“红色”，此处用比较级 more red than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
red 意为“红色”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最红色的一件，故用最高级 the most red door of the barn。
red 意为“红色”，母亲认为这件东西“太红色了，谁也用不上”，too red to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
red 意为“涨红”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩涨红的脸”，此处作前置定语 a red face of the boy。
red 意为“涨红”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩男孩涨红的脸一样涨红”，同级比较用 as red as。
red 意为“涨红”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“涨红的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something red。
red 意为“涨红”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当涨红”，quite 修饰原级 red。
red 意为“涨红”，1997 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要涨红”，故用比较级 more red than。
red 意为“涨红”，母亲 1999 年说的是“整个画室里最涨红的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most red face of the boy。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1987 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件红色的红门。（a red door of the barn）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更红色。（more red than …）
母亲觉得它太红色，谁也用不上。（too red to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩涨红的脸。（a red face of the boy）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩男孩涨红的脸一样涨红。（as red as …）
到了 1994 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件涨红的东西。（something red）
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a red door of the barn in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was more red than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too red to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a red face of the boy.
He said nobody would call it as red as the face of the boy they had once had.
By 1994 the catalogue asked for nothing but something red.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 red 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a red door of the barn in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most red door of the barn in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too red to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a red face of the boy, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite red, and everybody laughed.
The red ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
